name: Columbia Packaging Group
old_description: Custom printed bags and rollstock for brands that demand performance
about:
Columbia Packaging Group is headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri. The company was established in 2017 with a strategy to acquire and consolidate regional flexible packaging manufacturers, beginning with M&M Printed Bag and Packaging Materials Inc. (PMI). In 2020 it launched Biolo, a proprietary line of certified compostable packaging.

The company operates as a full-service flexible packaging manufacturer with in-house extrusion, flexographic printing, and converting capabilities. It runs production facilities in California and Ohio; the California site supports up to 60-inch web width and 8-color registered printing, while the Ohio site offers 6-color inline printing on webs from 3 to 47 inches. Capabilities include custom film extrusion from raw resin, slitting up to 10 rolls across, and precision bag making with numerous style options such as wicketed, zip-lock, and tamper-evident configurations.

Columbia Packaging Group serves a range of industries including fresh produce, food service, retail, agriculture, industrial and automotive, and towel and tissue. Its packaging solutions are used for clear produce bags, food-safe compostable straws, high-graphic retail bags, UV-resistant agricultural films, heavy-duty industrial part protection, and high-speed overwrap film for tissue lines.

The company emphasizes its differentiation through certified compostability (TÜV home and industrial), food-safety compliance (BRC, AIB, BPI), and operational reliability from resin to finished rollstock. The Biolo brand was created to deliver sustainable packaging that integrates with existing converting lines without sacrificing performance.

name: Commercial Foods
old_description: Find out what new items Commercial Foods is carrying for the 26-27 School year.
about:
Founded in 1984, Commercial Food Systems, Inc. is an Indiana-owned and operated food distribution company headquartered in Indianapolis. Anthony Gates serves as president of the business, which began with a focus on providing customer-centric service to institutional foodservice operators.

The company distributes a broad range of products including beverages, breakfast items, fruits, snacks, condiments, single-portion packs, bulk items, holiday cookies, concessions, signage, equipment, paper goods, and kitchen wares. It operates without contracts, minimum orders, or delivery and fuel surcharges, and provides an online ordering platform, procurement support, and nutritional documentation for compliance with programs such as Smart Snacks and Buy American.

Commercial Food Systems serves three primary segments: K-12 schools, day care centers, and health care facilities. Its customer base includes Indiana Educational Service Centers, the Greater Chicagoland area, and the western third of Ohio. Testimonials reference long-standing relationships with districts such as Jennings County Schools, Western Wayne, and Plainfield Community Schools.

The company cites its dedication to customer service and its role as a partner and industry advisory council member of the Indiana School Nutrition Association as key differentiators. It emphasizes a product portfolio built around compliant beverages, Smart Snacks, and small equipment, maintaining that its service model has remained consistent since its founding.

name: Common Species
old_description: Furniture design studio hand-building pieces in Longmont, Colorado
about:
Common Species operates from Longmont, Colorado, as a furniture design and production studio owned and operated by Sergei Parfenov. Parfenov brings a professional design background to the studio, which focuses on hand-building each piece with meticulous attention to detail.

The studio produces custom furniture for residential and commercial clients, including seating, tables, coffee and accent tables, storage, kitchen pieces, and built-ins. Every item is handmade using locally sourced materials and responsible practices, with hardware such as brass locking mechanisms, brass accents, and German-made extension hardware integrated into the designs. No facility size or headcount figures are disclosed.

Common Species serves both residential and commercial markets, delivering custom work tailored to individual homes and business spaces. The studio emphasizes pieces intended to become lasting parts of a home and to be passed through generations.

The company differentiates itself through its commitment to heirloom-quality craftsmanship, encouraging custom projects so that each piece reflects the owner's vision. Locally sourced materials and responsible production practices further define its approach.

name: Commonwealth Food Service Equipment
old_description: We are dedicated to serving the foodservice industry with integrity, providing valuable and trustworthy solutions to our customers.
about:
Commonwealth Food Service Equipment operates from Lexington, Kentucky. The company was founded by Stacey Landfield, who moved to Lexington in 1990 and later relaunched the business after the sale of her previous employer. A founding year is not publicly disclosed.

The firm provides end-to-end commercial kitchen solutions for Kentucky clients, covering design, procurement, delivery, installation, and ongoing maintenance. Its services include kitchen layout and workflow consulting, equipment sourcing with open-book pricing, installation of serving lines, walk-in refrigeration, cooking equipment, and modular shelving, plus same-day service triage through its Machine Kings division.

Primary customers include K–12 school districts such as Bowling Green Independent and Muhlenberg County, as well as restaurants, catering operations, senior living facilities, hotels, universities, hospitals, churches, casinos, and general business-and-industry sites. Testimonials cite school nutrition directors and a Lexington restaurant owner.

Commonwealth differentiates itself with a community-first, brand-agnostic approach: every quote presents three comparable options with total-cost transparency, labor rates are published, and a Right-Fit Guarantee promises remediation if equipment underperforms. The company also handles warranty registration, rebate and grant guidance, energy-efficient specifications, and responsible recycling.

name: Commonwealth Packaging Company
old_description: For over 60 years, Commonwealth Packaging Company has been leading the custom packaging industry by partnering with brand conscious companies to create special and memorable packaging.
about:
Commonwealth Packaging Company operates from Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. The firm traces its roots back more than six decades, though an exact founding year is not published. Ownership structure and founder names have not been disclosed publicly.

The company provides end-to-end custom packaging services, spanning design and program coordination, purchasing and sourcing, production management with in-house and third-party quality control, logistics, and bi-coastal storage and distribution. It manages a global manufacturing network of domestic and overseas factory partners and operates 80,000 square feet of warehouse space to support bulk ordering and nationwide redistribution.

Clients range from independent boutiques to global omni-channel retailers across retail, e-commerce, and hospitality sectors. A noted partner is Sant Ambroeus, a retail brand featured on the company's site.

Commonwealth Packaging emphasizes a hands-on approach, guiding customers through every step from concept to delivery. It leverages long-standing factory relationships to secure competitive pricing while maintaining quality, and manages freight directly for shipment visibility.

name: Compass Made
old_description: Electromechanical contract manufacturer specializing in cable/harness assembly
about:
Compass Made is headquartered in Fremont, California, with additional manufacturing facilities in Deming, New Mexico, and an engineering support center in Juárez, Mexico. The company traces its roots to 1979 when Compass Components, Inc. was founded to provide components, distribution, and assembly services to local customers. Over the decades the business expanded into contract manufacturing and cable and harness assembly, rebranding as Compass Made in 2018 to emphasize its focus on engineered solutions.

Today Compass Made operates as an electromechanical contract manufacturer specializing in cable and wire harness assemblies, electromechanical box builds, and large-scale system integration. Capabilities span design, engineering, prototyping, and full-rate production of harnesses, cables, and integrated assemblies.

The customer base includes industry leaders in transportation, semiconductor equipment, industrial machinery, agriculture, food processing, energy, and robotics. Compass Made also continues to function as a component distribution hub for regional companies, supplementing its contract manufacturing services.

The company cites its corporate values — integrity, respect, accountability, innovation, improvement, and customer focus — as the foundation of its differentiation. Leadership emphasizes that the engineering team is frequently engaged to help customers refine prototypes and improve manufacturability, positioning Compass Made as a solutions-oriented partner rather than a pure build-to-print shop.

name: Component Central Inc
old_description: We specialize in supplying commercial/military electronic components and fasteners to government agencies, OEMs, repair stations, and distributors. Hard to find and obsolete items are our specialty.
about:
Component Central Inc operates from Stanton, California, where it has established itself as a supplier of commercial and military electronic components and fasteners. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or the names of its founders.

The company’s core business is the distribution of a broad range of electronic parts, including capacitors, resistors, semiconductors, diodes, transistors, switches, connectors, relays, fasteners, and wire and cable. It stocks products from hundreds of manufacturers such as AVX, Kemet, Vishay, Texas Instruments, Amphenol, and 3M. Component Central emphasizes its ability to source hard-to-find and obsolete items, a niche that supports maintenance and repair operations for legacy systems. No details on facility size, headcount, or annual volume are provided.

Its customer base spans government agencies, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), repair stations, and other distributors. The company serves both commercial and military markets, providing components that meet military specifications where required. Concrete examples from its product listings show a focus on aerospace and defense-grade fasteners from brands like Boeing, Honeywell, and Huck, as well as electronic components from major semiconductor vendors.

Component Central positions its specialty in obsolete and hard-to-find items as its primary differentiator, aiming to be a reliable source for parts that are no longer in regular production. The company does not state a specific founding mission beyond this market focus.

name: Component Manufacturing Company
old_description: Custom Roof, Floor Trusses, and Wall Panels for Unmatched Quality and Efficiency
about:
Component Manufacturing Company operates from Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Founded by veteran Lloyd Reaves, who recognized the need for quality affordable housing and pioneered the application of bowstring truss technology to broader building components, the company is employee-owned. Reaves earned a patent for his innovations, establishing a foundation of "growth through excellence."

The company manufactures engineered wood trusses, floor systems, and wall panels at its Sioux Falls plant. Using advanced design software and automated production equipment, the team performs project analysis, site assessment, and delivery logistics planning. A triple-check quality system verifies each plan before fabrication, and timber is sourced from sustainable suppliers.

Component Manufacturing serves residential, commercial, and industrial construction markets. Recent projects include the Grand Living at Lake Lorraine development, the 610 West apartment complex in Minneapolis for Doran Companies, and the Willow Run community in Sioux Falls. Clients such as Heavy Constructors, Custom Touch, Big D Homes, Superior Homes, and Rallis Construction rely on the firm for structural components.

The company differentiates itself through its employee-ownership model, sustainable material sourcing, and a dedicated sales team that uses real-time technology to support customers. Its founding philosophy—driven by a veteran's insight into affordable housing—continues to guide a focus on innovation, efficiency, and rigorous attention to detail.
